# Azure AKS Automatic values

`azure-automatic.values.yaml` targets **Azure AKS Automatic** clusters. Download the raw file
from [`values/azure-automatic.values.yaml`](https://github.com/marketplace-specificai/specificai-platform/blob/main/values/azure-automatic.values.yaml),
fill in the `<PLACEHOLDER>` values it marks, and pass it to
`helm upgrade --install` as described in the [install guide](../install.md).

```yaml
# DO NOT EDIT in the public repository. This file is generated from
# SpecificAI's private chart sources by
# tools/marketplace_mirror/transform_content.py and republished on every
# chart release. Copy it, fill in the placeholder values it marks, and keep
# the copy under your own version control.

# ==============================================================================
# Cluster type: Azure AKS — Automatic (built-in node auto-provisioning)
# ==============================================================================
# WARNING: This file is for AKS Automatic ONLY. Helm has no way to detect which
# mode your cluster actually runs in. Applying this file to an AKS Standard
# cluster with pre-built node pools (or applying azure-standard.values.yaml
# here) can leave GPU pods pending indefinitely, because there is no
# controller in that cluster mode to satisfy the NodePool/AKSNodeClass this
# file relies on. Use azure-standard.values.yaml instead if your cluster has
# manually-provisioned GPU node pools.
# ==============================================================================
#
# AKS Automatic clusters run node auto-provisioning (NAP) out of the box, so
# the chart's own NodePool + AKSNodeClass resources are enough — no separate
# Karpenter install or IAM-style role is needed (unlike AWS self-managed
# Karpenter). NAP-provisioned GPU nodes come with the NVIDIA driver and device
# plugin preinstalled by the platform, so the chart's own device plugin
# DaemonSet must stay disabled. GPU tiers are selected by the provider-native
# `karpenter.azure.com/sku-name` label NAP applies to every node, rather than
# a pool label — there is no pre-built pool to label on this cluster mode.
#
# Generated by tools/marketplace_mirror/generate_customer_values.py from the
# chart's annotated values.yaml and profiles/azure-automatic.overlay.yaml. Do not edit
# by hand: change the annotation or the overlay, then regenerate.
#
# How to read this file:
#   - Live keys are what this cluster type needs. Replace every <YOUR_*>
#     placeholder before installing; the chart rejects any that remain.
#   - `# key: default` lines are optional settings, shown with the chart's
#     default. Uncomment a line (and its parent keys) only to change it --
#     anything left commented keeps tracking the chart default on upgrade.
#   - `# -- ...` lines describe the key below them.
#   - Credentials do not belong here: put them in a separate
#     secrets.values.yaml (see secrets.values.example.yaml) and pass both
#     files to helm.

global:
  # -- (REQUIRED) Cloud provider. One of: aws, azure, gcp, or empty string for single-node / bare-metal.
  cloudProvider: "azure"

  # Azure region your cluster runs in, e.g. southcentralus.
  cloudRegion: "<YOUR_AZURE_REGION>"

  # Storage account + container backing object storage, as "<account>/<container>".
  bucketName: "<YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME>/<YOUR_CONTAINER_NAME>"

  # Workload Identity (UAMI) client ID the platform's ServiceAccount uses.
  roleId: "<YOUR_MANAGED_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID>"

  # Hostname the platform will be served on.
  optuneAddress: "<YOUR_PLATFORM_HOSTNAME>" # e.g. specificai.yourcompany.com

  # -- Extra hostnames accepted by Gateway HTTPRoutes and host-aware OAuth (callback + post-login redirect). Keep optuneAddress / FRONTEND_URL on the live name.
  # additionalOptuneAddresses: []

  # -- Runtime environment prefix for message-broker topic names. Must match `common.env.data.RUNTIME_ENV`.
  # Used by the batch fetcher subcharts (teacher-fetcher, judgment-fetcher, generation-fetcher) to derive
  # their KEDA Kafka trigger topic (`<runtimeEnv>_<route>_batch_ready`) when `<subchart>.keda.topic` is unset.
  # runtimeEnv: ""

  # -- Default node selector applied to all workloads.
  # nodeSelector: {}

  # -- Node selector for CPU workloads.
  # cpuNodeSelector: {}

  # CPU tiers key off the "workload" label the chart's NodePool template
  # applies. Leaving these unset on Azure reaches job-runner as an empty
  # selector and the Job is silently never created, so they must be set
  # explicitly.
  cpuHighPerformanceNodeSelector:
    workload: "cpu-basic"

  # -- Node selector for basic CPU workloads. Defaults to `{"kubernetes.io/os":"linux"}` on GCP.
  cpuBasicNodeSelector:
    workload: "cpu-basic"

  # -- Node selector for low-performance CPU workloads. Defaults to `{"kubernetes.io/os":"linux"}` on GCP.
  cpuLowPerformanceNodeSelector:
    workload: "cpu-basic"

  # GPU tiers key off the native SKU-name label NAP applies to every node it
  # provisions, so you can pin exactly which VM SKU serves each tier without
  # depending on a pool label. Must match (or be a subset of)
  # common.karpenter.azure.gpu*SkuNames below.
  gpuHighPerformanceNodeSelector:
    karpenter.azure.com/sku-name: "<YOUR_HIGH_PERF_GPU_SKU>"  # e.g. Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4

  # -- Node selector for basic GPU workloads. Defaults to the `gpu-basic` GKE pool on GCP, or to the matching ComputeClass when `computeClasses.create` is enabled.
  gpuBasicNodeSelector:
    karpenter.azure.com/sku-name: "<YOUR_BASIC_GPU_SKU>"  # e.g. Standard_NV36ads_A10_v5

  # -- Node selector for low-performance GPU workloads. Defaults to the `gpu-low-performance` GKE pool on GCP, or to the matching ComputeClass when `computeClasses.create` is enabled.
  gpuLowPerformanceNodeSelector:
    karpenter.azure.com/sku-name: "<YOUR_LOW_PERF_GPU_SKU>"  # e.g. Standard_NC8as_T4_v3

  # -- Affinity rules applied to all workloads.
  # affinity: {}

  # -- Annotations added to all workloads.
  # annotations: {}

  # -- Extra labels added to all pods.
  # podLabels: {}

  # azure:
  #   useWorkloadIdentityForBlob: true

  # ingress:
  #   createIngress: true
  #   createCertificateSecret: false
  #   className: "nginx"
  #   certificateSecretName: ""

  gateway:
    # -- Use Kubernetes Gateway API instead of legacy Ingress (not both).
    enabled: false
    # -- Gateway resource name. Defaults to "<release>-gw" when empty.
    # name: ""
    # -- GatewayClassName (required when enabled). GKE: gke-l7-global-external-managed (Standard + Autopilot). k3s: traefik.
    # gatewayClassName: ""
    # -- Gateway metadata annotations. GCP: networking.gke.io/certmap for Certificate Manager TLS.
    # annotations: {}
    # oauth:
    #   splitMode: false
    #   pathPrefix: /api/auth
    # tls:
    #   secretName: ""
    #   createSecret: false
    # listeners:
    #   http:
    #     enabled: true
    #     port: 80
    #   https:
    #     enabled: true
    #     port: 443
    # redirectHttpToHttps: true

  # -- Create the platform K8s Secret from values under common.secrets.
  # createSecret: true

  # -- Name of the Secret to mount as envFrom across all pods.
  # envFromSecret: "specificai-secrets"

  # -- Name of the imagePullSecret for private registry access.
  # imagePullSecretsName: "docker-ro-creds"

  # -- Name of the SSO credentials Secret. Keys depend on IDP:
  #   Google: WEB_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, WEB_APP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, WEB_APP_GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI
  #   Azure:  WEB_APP_AZURE_CLIENT_ID, WEB_APP_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, WEB_APP_AZURE_REDIRECT_URI, WEB_APP_AZURE_TENANT_ID
  #   Okta:   WEB_APP_OKTA_CLIENT_ID, WEB_APP_OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET, WEB_APP_OKTA_REDIRECT_URI, WEB_APP_OKTA_ISSUER
  # optuneAuthSecretName: "specificai-auth-secret"

  # -- Create the platform ConfigMap from values under common.env.
  # createConfigMap: true

  # -- Name of the ConfigMap to mount as envFrom across all pods.
  # envFromConfigMap: "specificai-env"

  # -- Name of the ConfigMap the chart creates from common.env. Empty names it "<release>-env". Keep it equal to envFromConfigMap, the name pods mount.
  # envFromConfigMapName: ""

  # -- Name of the ConfigMap holding SSO/auth configuration.
  # optuneAuthConfigMapName: "specificai-auth-config"

  # -- Name of the Kubernetes ServiceAccount used by all platform pods.
  # serviceAccountName: specificai

  # -- Create a cluster-scoped ClusterRole for node reading. Keep true for single-platform-per-cluster.
  # createClusterRole: true

  # kedaRabbitmqAuth:
  #   existingSecret: ""
  #   passwordKey: "RABBITMQ_PASSWORD"
  #   usernameKey: ""
  # tolerations: []
  # gpuBasicTolerations: []
  # gpuLowPerformanceTolerations: []
  # gpuHighPerformanceTolerations: []

  # -- Coralogix region domain (e.g. `eu2.coralogix.com`, `cx498.coralogix.com`).
  # Same value as `specificai-observability.coralogix.global.domain`; when both are set, this one wins.
  # domain: "eu2.coralogix.com"

  # -- Cluster name reported to Coralogix as a resource attribute. Override per environment.
  # Same value as `specificai-observability.coralogix.global.clusterName`; when both are set, this one wins.
  # clusterName: "<REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_CLUSTER_NAME>"

  # -- Coralogix application name for logs none of the exporter's application_name_attributes resolve for.
  # Same value as `specificai-observability.coralogix.global.defaultApplicationName`; when both are set, this one wins.
  # defaultApplicationName: "otel"

  # -- Log level of the OpenTelemetry collectors themselves.
  # Same value as `specificai-observability.coralogix.global.logLevel`; when both are set, this one wins.
  # logLevel: "warn"

# Workload Identity is the default Blob auth on Azure (global.azure.useWorkloadIdentityForBlob),
# so both the backend models volume and Triton need the models container
# mounted directly rather than reading via an account key. Required on Azure
# regardless of cluster mode.
backend:
  # IAM role the backend assumes for Amazon Bedrock calls. Unset, it uses the
  # AWS credentials in the platform Secret. Never set it to "": an empty entry
  # here overrides one set through common.env.data or the platform Secret.
  # env:
  #   BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN: "arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<bedrock-role>"
  storage:
    # useCloudCsi: true
    # storageClassName: ""
    blob:
      # -- Azure Blob container the backend mounts for model storage (Blob CSI).
      containerName: "<YOUR_CONTAINER_NAME>"
      # secretName: "optune-storage-account-secret"
      # -- Azure Storage account holding that container.
      accountName: "<YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME>"
      # Resource group of the storage account (NOT the AKS MC_* group).
      resourceGroup: "<YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_RESOURCE_GROUP>"
  # replicaCount: 2

specificai-inference:
  enabled: true

  # Only on the legacy storage-account-key path (global.azure.useWorkloadIdentityForBlob:
  # false, models.blob.enabled: false), where Triton reads the models over as://:
  # storageProvider: "as"
  models:
    # deployedModelsPath: "deployed_models"
    blob:
      # -- Azure only: mount the models container into the Triton pod (Blob CSI + Workload Identity) and read the model repository from a local path instead of `as://`. Required on Azure while `global.azure.useWorkloadIdentityForBlob` is true, because the `as://` URI can only authenticate with a storage account key.
      enabled: true
      # -- Azure Storage account holding the models container. Required when `blob.enabled` is true.
      accountName: "<YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME>"
      # -- Blob container holding the deployed models. Required when `blob.enabled` is true.
      containerName: "<YOUR_CONTAINER_NAME>"
      # -- Resource group of the storage account (not the AKS `MC_*` group). Required when `blob.enabled` is true.
      resourceGroup: "<YOUR_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_RESOURCE_GROUP>"
      # -- Mount path for the models container inside the Triton pod. The model repository is `deployedModelsPath` under this.
      # mountPath: "/models"

  # serviceAccount:
  #   name: ""
  #   roleId: ""
  #   create: false
  # extraEnv: []

  # keda:
  #   enabled: false

  # monitoring:
  #   serviceMonitor:
  #     enabled: false
  #   grafanaDashboard:
  #     enabled: false
  #   alerts:
  #     enabled: false

  # ingress:
  #   path: /

specificai-vllm-inference:
  enabled: false
  # gpuTier: "gpu-basic"

  # model:
  #   gpuMemoryUtilization: 0.65

  # models:
  #   pvc:
  #     enabled: false
  #     blob:
  #       enabled: false
  #       accountName: ""
  #       containerName: ""
  #       resourceGroup: ""
  #       extraMountOptions: []

  # -- RabbitMQ the KEDA session-queue scaler connects to. Keep in step with the RABBITMQ_* keys under common.env.data.
  # rabbitmq:
  #   host: "specificai-rabbitmq"
  #   port: "5672"
  #   username: "specificai"
  #   vhost: "/"

  # keda:
  #   enabled: true

  # resources:

  #     nvidia.com/gpu: 1

  # ingress:
  #   enabled: false
  #   path: /public/playground

  # -- Prefix of the KEDA session-queue topic ("<runtimeEnv>_summarization_inference_session"). Keep equal to common.env.data.RUNTIME_ENV.
  # runtimeEnv: ""

# -- Isolated Triton replica used by POST /model-perf-runs (KEDA 0..1 per slot).
specificai-triton-perf-eval:
  enabled: false

  # keda:
  #   slotCount: 3

  # tiers:
  #   gpu-low-performance:
  #     enabled: true
  #   gpu-basic:

rabbitmq:
  enabled: true

  # auth:

  # resources:

  #     cpu: 250m

keda:

  # crds:

mongodb:

# kube-prometheus-stack:

common:
  # -- Annotations added to all common resources.
  # annotations: {}

  # env:
  #   data:
  #     MESSAGE_BROKER_TYPE: "rabbitmq"
  #     KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: ""
  #     KAFKA_ENV: cloud
  #     KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM: SCRAM-SHA-512
  #     KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL: SASL_SSL
  #     KAFKA_USERNAME: optune
  #     RABBITMQ_HOST: "specificai-rabbitmq"
  #     RABBITMQ_PORT: "5672"
  #     RABBITMQ_VHOST: "/"
  #     RABBITMQ_USERNAME: "specificai"
  #     RABBITMQ_EXCHANGE: "specificai"
  #     STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME: ""
  #     STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME: ""
  #     STORAGE_TYPE: "s3"
  #     DB_NAME: specificai
  #     RUNTIME_ENV: ""
  #     BATCH_POLLER_ENABLED: "true"
  #     TRITON_URL: http://specificai-specificai-inference:8000

  # -- SSO configuration. Set method and the matching WEB_APP_* keys for that IDP. BOTH is Google+Azure only and never includes Okta.
  optune_auth:
    # -- Enable SSO authentication.
    enabled: false
    # -- SSO method. One of: NONE, GOOGLE, AZURE, OKTA, BOTH (case-insensitive — backend normalizes to uppercase). OKTA is a first-class Helm IDP: set method=OKTA and the web_app_okta_* keys. BOTH stays Google+Azure only.
    # method: "NONE"
    # -- Frontend URL used as the OAuth redirect base.
    # frontend_url: ""
    # -- Okta OIDC client ID. Empty by default; required only when method is OKTA.
    # web_app_okta_client_id: ""
    # -- Okta OIDC redirect URI (https://<host>/api/auth/okta/callback on deployed installs).
    # web_app_okta_redirect_uri: ""
    # -- Okta issuer URL (full URL, typically https://<org>.okta.com/oauth2/default).
    # web_app_okta_issuer: ""
    # web_app_google_client_id: ""
    # web_app_google_redirect_uri: ""
    # web_app_azure_client_id: ""
    # web_app_azure_redirect_uri: ""
    # web_app_azure_tenant_id: ""

  # -- Karpenter NodePool / NodeClass rendering.
  karpenter:
    # Render the chart's NodePool + AKSNodeClass (see
    # charts/common/templates/nodepool.yaml + nodeclasses.yaml). AKS
    # Automatic's built-in NAP controller reconciles them directly — no
    # roleArn/discoveryTag needed (those are AWS-only concepts).
    createNodePools: true
    # -- Karpenter mode (AWS only). "self-managed" — chart renders EC2NodeClass + NodePools for in-cluster Karpenter. "auto-mode" — chart skips EC2NodeClass and renders NodePools using EKS Auto Mode's built-in default NodeClass.
    # mode: "self-managed"
    # -- Apply Mountpoint-S3 CSI startup taint `s3.csi.aws.com/agent-not-ready:NoExecute` on AWS Karpenter NodePools. Default false: pinned CSI v1.15 does not remove the taint, so GPU/CPU pods stay Pending. Set true only after upgrading Mountpoint-S3 CSI to >= 2.1.0.
    # s3CsiStartupTaint: false
    # SKUs NAP is allowed to provision per GPU tier — keep in sync with the
    # sku-name node selectors above. Empty lists fall back to the chart's
    # defaults (L40S for high, several A10 variants for basic, T4 for low).
    azure:
      gpuHighSkuNames:
        - "<YOUR_HIGH_PERF_GPU_SKU>"
      gpuBasicSkuNames:
        - "<YOUR_BASIC_GPU_SKU>"
      gpuLowSkuNames:
        - "<YOUR_LOW_PERF_GPU_SKU>"

  # NAP-provisioned GPU nodes come with the NVIDIA driver and device plugin
  # preinstalled by the platform — leave the chart's own DaemonSet disabled to
  # avoid double-managing the same device.
  nvidiaDevicePlugin:
    # -- Deploy the NVIDIA device plugin DaemonSet.
    enabled: false
    # -- Node labels that identify GPU workload node pools targeted by the DaemonSet.
    # workloadLabels:
    #   - gpu-high-performance
    #   - gpu-basic
    #   - gpu-low-performance

  # -- Coralogix app-side secret configuration.
  # coralogix:
  #   secret:
  #     create: true
  #     secretName: coralogix-keys

specificai-observability:
  # -- Deploy the SpecificAI observability stack (Coralogix OpenTelemetry agent → ships logs and metrics to Coralogix).
  enabled: true

  # coralogix:
  #   secret:
  #     create: false
  #     secretName: coralogix-keys
  #   global:
  #     domain: "eu2.coralogix.com"
  #     clusterName: "<REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_CLUSTER_NAME>"
  #     defaultApplicationName: "otel"
  #     logLevel: "warn"
  #   opentelemetry-agent:
  #     nodeSelector: {}
  #     affinity: {}
  #     config:
  #       exporters:
  #         coralogix:
  #           application_name_attributes:
  #             - "k8s.namespace.name"

reloader:
  # -- Enable Reloader (auto-restarts pods on ConfigMap/Secret changes).
  enabled: true

  # reloader:
  #   watchGlobally: true
  #   deployment:
  #     affinity: {}
  #     tolerations: []
```
